purpose: Story + psychology + commercial-narrative intelligence as ACTIVE cards the OS loads before any commercial edit, campaign, deck, caption, script, offer, or buyer-facing asset. Views over this store = the 8 libraries. Enforced by os_story_gate.py.

cards.title: But / Therefore (kill the AND THEN)
cards.problem: Edit/script feels like random B-roll or a list (this AND THEN this AND THEN this).
cards.when_to_use: Every commercial edit, video script, carousel, and deck sequence.
cards.story_principle: South Park rule (via Callaway): between every beat must sit BUT or THEREFORE, never AND THEN. Cause-and-effect, not a list.
cards.psychology_principle: Conflict opens a loop in the brain; context closes it. Open loops hold attention; a list closes nothing and bores.
cards.application: Storyboard each cut as a beat; write the connective. If two shots only connect with 'and then', cut one or reorder until it reads but/therefore.
cards.bad_output_prevented: Pretty-but-pointless montage; the #1 Gemini/operator complaint on Alma V1-V3.
cards.gate: STORY_GATE: sequence-logic check (why this shot before that shot).
cards.source: Storytelling game.docx (Callaway), Tip 1 'The Dance' + Matt Stone/Trey Parker NYU talk.
cards.alma_example: She arrives dragging a speaker (context) BUT the speaker fails her (conflict) THEREFORE the swimsuit is the calm center (resolution) BUT the world keeps interrupting (new loop). Not 'palm shot and then bikini and then trunk'.

cards.title: Open-Loop Hook (first 3 seconds)
cards.problem: Weak hook; viewer scrolls before the product appears.
cards.when_to_use: Opening 0-3s of every reel/ad; first line of every caption.
cards.story_principle: Open a loop the viewer needs closed: a question, an interruption, an incongruity (Callaway hook + the Dance).
cards.psychology_principle: Zeigarnik effect: unresolved tension is held in memory. Incongruity (luxury + awkward) forces a 'what is happening' reflex.
cards.application: Lead with the most incongruous real moment, not the prettiest. Withhold the resolution.
cards.bad_output_prevented: Opening on a generic pretty stand that promises nothing.
cards.source: Storytelling game.docx Tip 6 'The Hook' (Epic Gardening) + Tip 1 open loops.
cards.alma_example: Open on the deadpan woman dragging a rolling speaker across an empty Beverly Hills street (incongruity) or the walk-up lens-swipe (IMG_9510 ~15.4s) - both open a loop. NOT the static beauty stand.

cards.title: Rhythm / Length Variety (jagged edge)
cards.problem: Pacing feels monotonous or rushed; all cuts the same length.
cards.story_principle: Gary Provost: vary short/medium/long. Same-length beats drone; variety sings.
cards.psychology_principle: Predictable rhythm = subconscious boredom = churn. Variety re-captures attention.
cards.application: Edit: fast inserts 0.6-1.2s, action beats 1.5-2s, product/hero holds 2.5-4s. Never a flat 1.9s ASL. Caption: short lines, then one long one.
cards.bad_output_prevented: The 'rushed/flat pacing' note on Alma V3 (ASL 1.9s across the board).
cards.alma_example: Speaker gag quick (1.0-1.3s) BUT the trunk reveal and seated poster held long (3-4s) - the product is where the eye rests.

cards.title: Direct the Eye (the lit thing wins)
cards.problem: Eye doesn't land where intended; the product isn't the focal point.
cards.when_to_use: Every frame compose/crop/grade and reframe decision.
cards.story_principle: Callaway Tip 5: people look at the lit thing. Control the focal point.
cards.psychology_principle: Pre-attentive vision locks to the brightest/highest-contrast region first.
cards.application: Grade/crop so the swimsuit is the brightest, cleanest, highest-contrast element each beat; lower background exposure/saturation; punch-in if the product is small.
cards.bad_output_prevented: Busy frames where palms/car/sky steal from the suit.
cards.gate: STORY_GATE: visual hierarchy + 'product is the lit thing'.
cards.alma_example: On the palm-street wide (IMG_9511), punch-in so the suit reads; vignette + product-pop grade so she is the lit center, not the road.

cards.title: One-Friend Tone (drop the sell-barrier)
cards.problem: Copy/voiceover feels like an ad; viewer's 'am I being sold' guard goes up.
cards.when_to_use: Captions, scripts, DMs, deck voice, landing copy.
cards.story_principle: Callaway Tip 3 (Jobs/Neistat/Chamberlain): write to ONE close friend; conversational tone breaks the conscious identity barrier.
cards.psychology_principle: When it feels like a conversation, the viewer forgets they are an audience and lowers persuasion-resistance.
cards.application: Write captions as a text to one person; no marketing voice; no em-dashes; declarative + intimate.
cards.bad_output_prevented: Stiff brand-marketing captions that read AI-written.
cards.gate: STORY_GATE: feel check (what is the viewer meant to feel) + voice gate.
cards.alma_example: Caption: 'A strangely difficult day in a very good swimsuit.' Reads like a friend, not a brand.

cards.title: Closed Loop Ending (payoff + button)
cards.problem: Ending has no payoff; reel just stops.
cards.when_to_use: Final 3-5s of every edit; last line of copy.
cards.story_principle: Callaway Tip 4 'Direction': the piece is designed to land; the last beat closes the loop the hook opened (or loops back to it).
cards.psychology_principle: Resolution gives the dopamine of a closed loop; a strong final image becomes the memory and the share-trigger.
cards.application: End on the strongest HELD hero/poster frame, not a drive-off or a fade. Button it (freeze + logo + sound hit).
cards.bad_output_prevented: The 'weak payoff' note; ending on a tiny drive-off (Alma V1).
cards.gate: STORY_GATE: payoff = longest cleanest hero beat near the end.
cards.alma_example: End on D94A3310 seated-on-Mercedes held 3.5s + Alma Love lockup + shutter/boom - the poster that closes the 'will the suit survive the chaos' loop.

cards.title: Flawed Protagonist in a Built World
cards.problem: Model is pretty but there is no character; the brand has no point of view.
cards.when_to_use: Brand story, campaign concept, video premise, character/world rules.
cards.story_principle: Achebe (Things Fall Apart): a vivid protagonist defined by ONE governing trait (Okonkwo's rigid pride), set in a fully-ruled world; the drama is the trait tested by change.
cards.psychology_principle: Audiences bond to a clear, consistent character and project onto a flaw; a 'type' is more memorable than a pretty blank.
cards.application: Give the model a governing trait + a world with rules. Keep the character consistent across every shot.
cards.bad_output_prevented: Generic 'attractive person in nice place' content with no identity.
cards.source: Achebe, Things Fall Apart (Okonkwo as governing-trait protagonist; Umuofia as fully-ruled world).
cards.alma_example: Alma = a composed, mannequin-still woman (governing trait: unbreakable poise) in a luxury world that keeps malfunctioning. Her flaw/charm = she never reacts. The suit is her armor.

cards.title: Establish the World's Rules, Then Break One
cards.problem: Surreal/AI/deadpan beats feel random instead of meaningful.
cards.when_to_use: Concept, AI-world extension, surreal bumpers, deadpan comedy.
cards.story_principle: Achebe: the power of the fall comes from first showing the world's order (custom, proverb, ritual) so the break lands. Set normal, then violate it.
cards.psychology_principle: Incongruity only reads as meaning when there is an established baseline to violate.
cards.application: Show the luxury baseline (clean Canon beauty) BEFORE the chaos (iPhone weirdness) so the weird reads as story, not noise.
cards.bad_output_prevented: Random weird inserts that feel like an AI glitch instead of intentional deadpan.
cards.gate: STORY_GATE: world-logic (what is established, what is broken).
cards.source: Achebe, Things Fall Apart (order established then undone).
cards.alma_example: Beat 1-2 establish luxury composure (palm stillness, clean suit) THEREFORE the speaker drag/kick (rule-break) reads as deadpan comedy, not a mistake.

cards.title: Status / New-Luxury Signal
cards.problem: Work looks cheap; doesn't trigger desire or 'I want to be her'.
cards.when_to_use: Brand campaign, pricing, ICP, photo/video package, deck.
cards.story_principle: The aspirational figure must signal a status the buyer wants to borrow.
cards.psychology_principle: Trading Up (Silverstein) + status psychology: buyers pay premiums for emotional/identity benefits; luxury cues (Mercedes, Beverly Hills, poise) transfer status to the suit.
cards.application: Every frame must carry a status cue (chrome, palms, composure, clean grade). Remove anything that reads cheap (harsh blow-out, messy crop, visible plate).
cards.bad_output_prevented: Content that looks like a phone snapshot instead of a campaign.
cards.source: SNIPED corpus: sniped-new-luxury (Silverstein Trading Up), sniped-status-psychology.
cards.alma_example: The seated-on-Mercedes poster transfers Beverly-Hills status onto a swimsuit a mid-market buyer can actually afford = the trade-up.

cards.title: Withhold then Reveal (desire by delay)
cards.problem: Product shown flat and immediately; no build, no wanting.
cards.when_to_use: Edit sequencing, product reveal timing, carousel order.
cards.story_principle: Tension is created by delaying the thing the viewer wants to see clearly.
cards.psychology_principle: Anticipation > consumption for desire; a delayed clean product reveal is wanted more.
cards.application: Tease the suit (dangle/blur/partial) before the clean hero hold. The product PAUSE is the reward.
cards.bad_output_prevented: Front-loading the clean product so there is nothing to wait for.
cards.gate: STORY_GATE: what is withheld / what is revealed.
cards.source: Storytelling game open-loops + SNIPED hit-mechanics (Thompson, MAYA).
cards.alma_example: Bikini-dangle tease (IMG_9539) and lens-swipe blur BEFORE the clean trunk back-reveal hold (D94A3308 4.4s).

cards.title: Why They Buy Again (trust + hospitality)
cards.problem: One-off deliverable; no reason for the client to return.
cards.when_to_use: Client package, offer, post-delivery, case study.
cards.story_principle: The client buys the FEELING of being made to look like a real brand, repeatedly.
cards.psychology_principle: Trust Equation (credibility x reliability x intimacy / self-orientation) + Unreasonable Hospitality: exceed the promise once and they re-buy.
cards.application: Deliver more than asked (brand kit, preset, poster) so the client experiences elevation, not just photos.
cards.bad_output_prevented: Transactional handoff that doesn't earn the next booking.
cards.alma_example: Alma got a logo + signature LUT/preset + poster she did not ask for = she returns because we made her a brand, not a gallery.

cards.title: Specific Detail = Belief
cards.problem: Generic visuals/copy; nothing concrete to believe or remember.
cards.when_to_use: Insert selection, caption nouns, detail crops.
cards.story_principle: Concrete specific details (a chrome detail, red heels, a chain glint) make a world believable; but do not stack detail-on-detail (Callaway warns it kills the loop).
cards.psychology_principle: Concrete specifics are encoded and recalled; abstractions are not.
cards.application: Use 1-2 sharp detail inserts (lipstick, strap, chrome) as punctuation, not a pile. Caption with specific nouns.
cards.bad_output_prevented: Either generic wides OR an over-stuffed detail montage.
cards.gate: STORY_GATE: detail used as punctuation, not filler.
cards.source: Storytelling game.docx Tip 1 (detail-after-detail warning) + specificity principle.
cards.alma_example: ONE lipstick/jewelry close (IMG_9534 12.8s) and ONE strap detail - not ten product macros.

cards.title: Built-to-Spread (hit mechanics)
cards.problem: Good edit, no reason to share or rewatch.
cards.when_to_use: Reel concept, rollout, thumbnail, caption CTA.
cards.story_principle: A hit needs a familiar form with a surprising twist (MAYA) and a clear emotional broadcast.
cards.psychology_principle: Thompson Hit Makers: exposure + familiarity-with-a-twist drive spread; high-arousal emotion (awe, amusement) drives sharing.
cards.application: Make it a recognizable swimwear-ad form with the deadpan twist; engineer one rewatch detail (the kick, the freeze).
cards.bad_output_prevented: Technically clean but forgettable, unshareable content.
cards.alma_example: Familiar luxury-swimwear ad BUT she deadpan-kicks a broken speaker = the amusement twist people rewatch and tag.

cards.title: Name the Feeling (first-3-seconds intent)
cards.problem: No defined emotional target; the piece is technically fine but cold.
cards.when_to_use: Before any edit/caption/deck; the first decision.
cards.story_principle: Decide the single feeling the first 3 seconds must create, then engineer toward it.
cards.psychology_principle: Emotion precedes and drives attention + memory + action; undirected content produces no feeling.
cards.application: Write the target feeling at the top of every plan (e.g. 'amused intrigue + expensive calm'). Every beat serves it.
cards.bad_output_prevented: Edits assembled by 'looks good' with no emotional spine.
cards.alma_example: First 3s target = 'wait, what is she doing? (amused) and... she looks expensive (envy).' Hook chosen to produce exactly that.

cards.title: The Proverb (memorable compression)
cards.problem: Brand line/caption is forgettable; nothing to repeat.
cards.when_to_use: Tagline, end-card line, caption button, deck headline.
cards.story_principle: Achebe: 'proverbs are the palm-oil with which words are eaten' - compressed, image-rich phrases carry meaning and stick.
cards.psychology_principle: Compressed, concrete, rhythmic phrases are memorable and repeatable (the share unit).
cards.application: End on one proverb-like line, image-rich and short, not a feature list.
cards.gate: STORY_GATE (copy mode): one memorable line present.
cards.alma_example: 'The suit survived the chaos.' / 'Made for heat, movement, and beautifully awkward exits.'

cards.title: Motivated Cuts / VFX Only
cards.story_principle: Every cut/effect must be motivated by action or story (cut on action, wipe on a real object crossing lens).
cards.psychology_principle: Unmotivated flash/whip breaks immersion and reads amateur; motivated transitions are invisible.
cards.application: 80% hard cuts on action. Designed transition only at section breaks / on a real lens-cross. No vanity effects.
cards.bad_output_prevented: The 'transitions distracting' note (Gemini on Alma V3).
cards.alma_example: Use the REAL lens-swipe (IMG_9510 15.4s) as the only wipe; everything else hard-cuts on action.
